title: Pre-Launch Security Assessment for LLM Features
summary: Test a new chatbot, copilot or LLM feature for prompt injection, cross-customer data leakage, off-policy answers and unsafe output handling before release, with evidence and a retest.

seo.title: Pre-Launch Security Testing for LLM Features | VipraTech
seo.description: Security assessment of fintech LLM features before launch: prompt injection, cross-account data leakage, jailbreaks and output handling, mapped to OWASP.

designed_for: CISO or Head of Information Security

problem.intro: Fintech teams are adding LLM assistants to apps and merchant dashboards: transaction search, spend summaries, support chat and dispute help. These features read customer data and sometimes call internal APIs, so a well-crafted prompt can become a data breach. Traditional penetration tests and scanners do not test how the model behaves.

pain_points.title: Cross-customer data exposure
pain_points.detail: A model with access to a transaction API may return another user's data if authorisation is enforced in the prompt instead of the tool layer.

pain_points.title: Indirect prompt injection
pain_points.detail: Merchant names, UPI notes, uploaded documents and email content can carry instructions that the model follows.

pain_points.title: Off-policy answers
pain_points.detail: Assistants drift into investment advice, invented fee waivers or confident wrong statements about refunds, creating conduct and complaint risk.

pain_points.title: No evidence for launch approval
pain_points.detail: Risk committees and partner banks ask what was tested before launch, and teams have no structured answer.

solution.overview: We run a time-boxed security assessment of your LLM feature in a staging environment before it reaches customers. First we map the feature: model, system prompt, retrieval sources, tools and the data each can reach. Then we test it against the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications with automated attack libraries and manual, multi-turn attempts written for payments: injection through transaction notes and merchant names, attempts to read other accounts, system prompt extraction, jailbreaks towards financial advice and unsafe rendering of model output in your UI. Every finding comes with the exact prompts and responses, a severity rating and a practical fix. After you fix, we retest.
capabilities: Architecture and data-flow review of prompts, retrieval sources, tools and permissions
Automated attack runs for prompt injection, jailbreaks and system prompt extraction
Manual multi-turn testing with payments-specific scenarios in English, Hindi and Hinglish
Authorisation testing of every tool and API the model can call, using paired test accounts
Output-handling checks for script injection, link injection and markdown rendering in your UI
Findings report mapped to OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, followed by a retest

workflow.title: Scope and threat model
workflow.detail: We agree the feature, environment, test accounts and rules of engagement, and map what data and tools the model can reach.

workflow.title: Automated attack runs
workflow.detail: Attack libraries send large sets of injection, jailbreak and extraction prompts to the staging endpoint.

workflow.title: Manual scenario testing
workflow.detail: Testers run multi-turn, payments-specific attacks, including indirect injection through data fields the model reads.

workflow.title: Validate and rate
workflow.detail: Each suspected issue is reproduced, confirmed and rated by impact and likelihood.

workflow.title: Report and brief
workflow.detail: You receive findings with evidence and fixes, plus a briefing for engineering and risk.

workflow.title: Retest
workflow.detail: After fixes, we rerun the failed cases and record which issues are closed.

faqs.q: How is this different from our annual penetration test?
faqs.a: A standard pentest checks the web app, APIs and infrastructure. This assessment tests how the model behaves: whether prompts can override instructions, leak data through tools or produce unsafe output. You need both.

faqs.q: Do you need access to production?
faqs.a: No. We test in staging with synthetic accounts. If staging differs from production in prompts, models or tools, we record that as a limitation in the report.

faqs.q: Which models and providers do you cover?
faqs.a: Any LLM behind an HTTP endpoint, including Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini and self-hosted open-weight models. The method depends on your feature's design, not the provider.

faqs.q: Can you test in Hindi and Hinglish?
faqs.a: Yes. Guardrails are often weaker in Indian languages and code-mixed text, so our playbooks include Hindi and Hinglish attacks by default.
